summary: The openlit->OTEL migration is complete and the emitter already produces everything the request asks for: a USD cost counter, token histograms and request/error counters, every one of them labelled with parrot.agent.name, gen_ai.request/response.model and gen_ai.provider.name. Nothing needs to be instrumented. The gap is entirely at the two ends: (1) env/.env has telemetry switched OFF and aimed at OpenLIT's 4318 rather than the Prometheus OTLP receiver on 9090, which live Prometheus confirms by holding zero gen_ai_*/parrot_* series; and (2) both shipped example dashboards query metric names that no code path emits — one set belongs to the non-OTel PrometheusUsageRecorder, the other set never existed at all — and neither has a single by-agent panel. The work is therefore a wiring change plus a dashboard rewrite against the real instrument catalog, following the Codex integration landed days ago as a working template.

constraints.statement: Metrics can be pushed to exactly ONE OTLP endpoint (config.otlp_endpoint); only traces honour OTLP_TARGETS. Pointing otlp_endpoint at Prometheus without redirecting traces leaves every trace export POSTing to a non-existent /api/v1/otlp/v1/traces.

OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is a BASE URL — the exporters append /v1/metrics and /v1/traces themselves. For the Prometheus receiver the correct value is http://localhost:9090/api/v1/otlp, not the full .../v1/metrics path.

gen_ai.client.token.usage is a HISTOGRAM recorded twice per call (input then output). A token total must come from its _sum series; no token _total counter exists, which is precisely what parrot-overview.json wrongly assumes.

parrot.client.round.token.usage is a separate instrument and must never be summed together with gen_ai.client.token.usage — FEAT-397 kept them apart specifically to avoid double-counting rounds against call totals.

user_id and session_id are span attributes only and are deliberately excluded from metric labels for cardinality reasons, so per-user usage is NOT answerable from Prometheus — only per-agent, per-model, per-provider.

Cost is computed in-process by CostCalculator and emitted as the gen_ai.client.cost.total counter in USD with the full agent/model/provider label set, so cost panels are a direct sum, not a PromQL price join.
cost_usd() returns None for an unpriced model and that call silently adds nothing to the cost counter, so a cost dashboard needs a companion request-count panel to make unpriced models visible.

env/.env is git-ignored (.gitignore:181) and holds live API keys and AWS credentials. Changing it is an operator action on this host, not a committed diff, and its contents must never be reproduced in an SDD artifact.
metric_export_interval_ms defaults to 60000 and has no env var, so a freshly-wired dashboard stays empty for up to a minute after the first LLM call.

Dotted OTel names become Prometheus names via UnderscoreEscapingWithSuffixes (dots to underscores plus unit and _total suffixes), so the series will be shaped like gen_ai_client_request_count_total and gen_ai_client_token_usage_tokens_bucket — but the exact rendering of the USD unit on gen_ai.client.cost.total must be read off the live TSDB after the first export rather than assumed.

The Grafana dashboard provider is named claudestats and files everything into a folder literally called 'Claude Code' with foldersFromFilesStructure:false, so a parrot dashboard dropped in as-is lands in a misleadingly named folder.
Provisioned dashboards are read-only in the UI (allowUiUpdates:false); operators must 'Save as' to customise, which matters for how the dashboard is delivered.

docker/ currently has uncommitted work (modified README/compose/prometheus.yml plus untracked otel-collector.yml) introducing the Codex collector. Any change here must be sequenced against that dirty state rather than assuming a clean tree.
29 unit test modules under tests/unit/observability already assert the env contract, multi-target wiring and instrument names, so the emitter side is protected but also rigid.

hypotheses.statement: No instrumentation work and no architecture change. Move the existing env/.env [observability] variables from OpenLIT to Prometheus: OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED=true, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9090/api/v1/otlp, OBSERVABILITY_SAMPLING=0.0 to silence traces (enable_traces is not env-settable), and delete the deprecated no-op OBSERVABILITY_OPENLIT. Then replace both example dashboards with one written against the real instrument catalog, adding the by-agent dimension that has existed since FEAT-228 but was never surfaced.
hypotheses.reasoning: Every metric the request names already exists with the right labels, the target stack already accepts OTLP push and already serves two other producers end to end, and live Prometheus proves the only missing link is the producer.

hypotheses.statement: Rejected by the requester: route parrot through an OTel Collector that fans metrics to Prometheus and traces to OpenLIT. Retained only as the fallback if direct-push temporality fails.
hypotheses.reasoning: Costs one more container but keeps a single endpoint in .env, isolates parrot from Prometheus receiver quirks, and matches the pattern already proven for Codex — at the price of the collector's in-memory state resetting counters on restart.

hypotheses.statement: Alternative: switch OBSERVABILITY_BACKEND to prometheus and let Prometheus scrape the PrometheusUsageRecorder on :9464, which would make parrot-usage.json's parrot_llm_* queries correct as written.
hypotheses.reasoning: Cheapest dashboard fix but a functional regression: that recorder labels only (provider, model), so it cannot answer 'by agent' at all, and it abandons traces and the per-round instruments.

in_scope: env/.env [observability] block: move the existing variables from OpenLIT to Prometheus and enable telemetry (operator action on this host)
Silence traces via OBSERVABILITY_SAMPLING=0.0 within the same env move, since enable_traces is not env-settable
A new/rewritten Grafana dashboard whose PromQL matches the real instrument catalog, with total / by-agent / by-model / by-provider / cost panels
Placement of that dashboard so the running parrot-grafana provisions it, plus a sane Grafana folder
Updating docs/architecture/10-observability.md and the examples README to match the new wiring
Deleting or fixing the two stale example dashboards so they stop advertising non-existent metrics
out_of_scope: Any change to MetricsSubscriber instruments or labels — the emitter is complete
Per-user or per-session dashboards — deliberately not available in metrics
Removing the OpenLIT stack or the ai-parrot-openlit-bridge package
Alerting rules, recording rules, long-term storage or auth/TLS on the local stack
Multi-destination export (OTLP_TARGETS), any new collector service, or a code change to make enable_traces env-settable

unknowns.question: Once metrics point at Prometheus, where should traces go — OpenLIT via OTLP_TARGETS, a collector that fans out, or should traces be turned off on this host?
unknowns.user_answer: REVISED by requester: a straight move of the existing env variables from OpenLIT to Prometheus. No OTLP_TARGETS split, no collector. Traces silenced within the same env move via OBSERVABILITY_SAMPLING=0.0, since enable_traces is not env-settable (F014).

unknowns.question: Which artifact is 'the example grafana dashboard' to update — the two files in the package examples directory, a new file provisioned into the running parrot-grafana, or both kept in sync?
unknowns.user_answer: Both — a new provisioned dashboard in docker/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/ AND replace the two stale package-example files with the same JSON

unknowns.question: Direct OTLP push from parrot to Prometheus:9090, or route parrot through an OTel Collector like Codex does?
unknowns.user_answer: Direct OTLP push to http://localhost:9090/api/v1/otlp — pure env change, no new container; collector stays as documented fallback only if cumulative temporality fails.

unknowns.question: Should the parrot dashboard live in the existing 'Claude Code' Grafana folder, or should a second provisioning provider create an 'AI-Parrot' folder?
unknowns.user_answer: New 'AI-Parrot' folder via a second provider entry in dashboards.yml

unknowns.question: Since env/.env is git-ignored, should this feature also add a committed, secret-free template documenting the [observability] block?
unknowns.user_answer: Both — a committed secret-free example env file and the matching block in docs/architecture/10-observability.md

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence and complete — the emitter needs no change, the exact files, env vars, instrument names and provisioning paths are all identified, and a working precedent (the Codex dashboard) exists. What remains is a handful of configuration decisions, which is exactly what a spec resolves.
